title: NEET (UG) 2026 · 21 June 2026 (re-exam) · Code 50
instr: NEET (UG) 2026 re-examination held on 21 June 2026, Test Booklet Code 50, with the final answer key published by the National Testing Agency (NTA).
180 compulsory questions: Physics 1–45, Chemistry 46–90, Biology 91–180. Each has four options (1)–(4) with one correct answer.
Marking: +4 for a correct answer, −1 for a wrong answer, 0 if not answered. Total 720 marks.

source: Questions: NEET (UG) 2026 re-examination, Test Booklet Code 50. Answers: NTA final answer key. Explanations: All in All Exam Practice.

questions.text: A particle of mass $M$ moves along a horizontal $x$ axis from $x = 0$ to $x = L$. The coefficient of kinetic friction varies as a function of $x$ as $\mu_k(x) = \mu_0 - \alpha x$, where $\mu_0$, $\alpha$ are constants of appropriate dimensions, so that $\mu_k(L) = 0$. The total work done by the frictional force during the motion is $n\mu_0 MgL$, where $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity. The value of $n$ is:
questions.sol:
$\mu_k(L)=0$ gives $\alpha = \mu_0/L$, so $\mu_k$ falls linearly from $\mu_0$ to $0$.
Magnitude of work $= \int_0^L \mu_k Mg\,dx = Mg\left(\mu_0 L - \dfrac{\alpha L^2}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\mu_0 MgL$.
Hence $n = \dfrac{1}{2}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The mean free path of molecules in an ideal gas $A$ is half that of another ideal gas $B$. The diameter of the spherical molecules of gas $A$ is twice the diameter of the molecules of $B$. If number densities of the gases $A$ and $B$ are $n_A$ and $n_B$, respectively, the correct option is:
questions.sol:
$\lambda = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}\,\pi d^2 n}$, so $n = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}\,\pi d^2 \lambda}$.
$\dfrac{n_A}{n_B} = \dfrac{d_B^2\,\lambda_B}{d_A^2\,\lambda_A} = \dfrac{1}{4}\times 2 = \dfrac{1}{2}$.
So $n_A = \dfrac{1}{2}n_B$.

questions.text:
Two identical inductors are connected in two different configurations $P$ and $Q$, where a time varying current $I(t)$ is flowing, as shown in the figure. The induced emf between points $a$ and $b$ for configuration $P$ is $E_P$ and that for configuration $Q$ is $E_Q$. The ratio $E_P/E_Q$ is:
[Neglect the effect of mutual inductance.]
questions.sol:
In $P$, points $a$ and $b$ span only one inductor carrying the full current: $E_P = L\dfrac{dI}{dt}$.
In $Q$, the two inductors are in parallel between $a$ and $b$: $L_{eq} = L/2$, so $E_Q = \dfrac{L}{2}\dfrac{dI}{dt}$.
$E_P/E_Q = 2$.

questions.text: For sound waves, if the number of nodes for the 5$^{\text{th}}$ harmonic of an open-ended pipe is $n$ and that for the 9$^{\text{th}}$ harmonic of the same pipe with one of its ends closed is $m$, the ratio $\dfrac{n}{m}$ is
questions.sol:
Open pipe, $k$-th harmonic: $k$ (pressure) nodes $\Rightarrow n = 5$.
Closed pipe, harmonic number $2p-1$ has $p$ nodes; $9 = 2p-1 \Rightarrow p = 5$, so $m = 5$.
$n/m = 1$.

questions.text: Consider a long solenoid of length $l$ and radius $r$. If $n$ is the number of turns per unit length and $\mu_0$ is the permeability of free space, the inductance of the solenoid is :
questions.sol:
Field inside $B = \mu_0 nI$; flux linkage $N\Phi = (nl)(\mu_0 nI)(\pi r^2)$.
$L = N\Phi/I = \mu_0\pi n^2 r^2 l$.

questions.text: Consider a particle moving along a straight line, whose position as a function of time is given by $s(t) = \alpha t^2 - \beta t + \gamma$, where $\alpha = 1\ \text{ms}^{-2}$, $\beta = 6\ \text{ms}^{-1}$ and $\gamma = 5$ m. The average speed of the particle, in $\text{ms}^{-1}$ from $t = 0$ to $t = 6$ s is:
questions.sol:
$s = t^2 - 6t + 5$, $v = 2t - 6$, so the particle reverses at $t = 3$ s.
$s(0) = 5$, $s(3) = -4$, $s(6) = 5$ m. Distance $= 9 + 9 = 18$ m.
Average speed $= 18/6 = 3\ \text{ms}^{-1}$.

Take masses of $^{238}$U, $^{234}$Th and $^{4}$He as 238.050 u, 234.043 u and 4.003 u, respectively. The $Q$ value for the reaction, in keV, is:

questions.text: A beam of light falls on a metal surface such that photo-electrons are generated. If power of the light source starts to decrease linearly with time $t$, then variation of the photocurrent $I$ and magnitude of the stopping potential $|V|$ with time is best represented by:
questions.sol:
Photocurrent is proportional to the number of photons per second, i.e. to the power, so $I$ decreases linearly with $t$.
Stopping potential depends only on frequency ($e|V| = h\nu - \phi$), which is unchanged, so $|V|$ stays constant.
This matches option (1).

questions.text: Three identical capacitors, $P$, $Q$ and $S$, each of the capacitance $C$, are connected to a battery of voltage $V$, as shown in the figure. If the energy stored in the capacitor $P$ and total energy stored in the system are $U_P$ and $U_T$, respectively, then the ratio $\dfrac{U_P}{U_T}$ is:
questions.sol:
$P$ and $Q$ in series (each gets $V/2$) are in parallel with $S$ (gets $V$).
$U_P = \dfrac{1}{2}C\left(\dfrac{V}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{CV^2}{8}$; $U_T = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{C}{2} + C\right)V^2 = \dfrac{3CV^2}{4}$.
$U_P/U_T = 1/6$.

questions.text:
Water flows in a streamline motion through a horizontal pipe of circular cross-section as shown in the figure. The pressure difference of water between $P$ and $Q$ is 15 Nm$^{-2}$. The area of cross-section at $P$ and $Q$ are 40 cm$^2$ and 20 cm$^2$, respectively. The rate of flow of water through the pipe, in cm$^3$s$^{-1}$, is:
[Take density of water = 1000 kg m$^{-3}$]
questions.sol:
Continuity: $v_Q = 2v_P$.
Bernoulli: $\Delta p = \dfrac{1}{2}\rho(v_Q^2 - v_P^2) = \dfrac{3}{2}\rho v_P^2 \Rightarrow 15 = 1500\,v_P^2 \Rightarrow v_P = 0.1$ m/s.
Flow rate $= A_P v_P = 40\ \text{cm}^2 \times 10\ \text{cm/s} = 400\ \text{cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A current $I_0$ flows through a metallic circular loop of radius $r$ as shown in the figure. Resistance of the segment $ABC$ is half that of $ADC$. Magnitude of magnetic field at the centre $O$ of the loop is :
questions.sol:
The two semicircles are in parallel; current divides inversely as resistance: $I_{ABC} = \dfrac{2I_0}{3}$, $I_{ADC} = \dfrac{I_0}{3}$.
Each semicircle gives $\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4r}$ at $O$, in opposite directions.
$B = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4r}\left(\dfrac{2I_0}{3} - \dfrac{I_0}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_0}{12r}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In the measurement of viscosity of liquids using terminal velocity experiment, spherical balls of same radius but having different densities are used. The variation of the terminal velocity ($v$) with the ratio of density of spherical ball ($\sigma$) to density of the liquid ($\rho$), is best represented by:
questions.sol:
$v = \dfrac{2r^2(\sigma - \rho)g}{9\eta} = \dfrac{2r^2\rho g}{9\eta}\left(\dfrac{\sigma}{\rho} - 1\right)$.
For $\sigma/\rho \le 1$ the ball does not sink, so there is no (downward) terminal velocity; beyond 1, $v$ rises linearly from zero.
This is graph (1).

questions.text: Two planets $P_1$ and $P_2$ with equal mass have radii $R_1$ and $R_2$, respectively, where $R_2 = \dfrac{R_1}{2}$. The escape speeds of $P_1$ and $P_2$ are $v_1$ and $v_2$, respectively. Then $\dfrac{v_2}{v_1}$ is:
questions.sol:
$v_e = \sqrt{2GM/R}$; with equal $M$, $v_e \propto 1/\sqrt{R}$.
$\dfrac{v_2}{v_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{R_1}{R_2}} = \sqrt{2}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a solar system, the time-period of revolution of a planet tracing a circular orbit of radius $R$ is proportional to:
questions.sol:
Gravity provides centripetal force: $\dfrac{GMm}{R^2} = m\omega^2 R \Rightarrow T^2 = \dfrac{4\pi^2}{GM}R^3$.
So $T \propto R^{3/2}$ (Kepler's third law).

questions.text:
Two infinitely long parallel conducting wires $A$ and $B$ carry currents $I$ and $2I$, respectively, in the same direction. The wire $A$ has uniform mass per unit length $\lambda$ and lies on an insulated floor. The wire $B$ is kept fixed at a height $h$ above the floor. The minimum magnitude of $h$ so that the wire $A$ does not rise from the floor is:
[$g$ is the acceleration due to gravity and $\mu_0$ is the permeability of free space.]
questions.sol:
Parallel currents attract, so $A$ is pulled upward with force per length $\dfrac{\mu_0 (I)(2I)}{2\pi h} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{\pi h}$.
$A$ stays on the floor if $\dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{\pi h} \le \lambda g$, i.e. $h \ge \dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{\pi\lambda g}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An ideal Zener diode with breakdown voltage of $-3$ V is reverse biased with a negative input voltage $V_i = -5$ V. The magnitude of voltage difference between point $B$ and $A$ is:
questions.sol:
The 5 V input exceeds the 3 V breakdown, so the Zener conducts and holds 3 V across $C$–$B$.
The rest of the supply drops across $R$ (between $B$ and $A$): $5 - 3 = 2$ V.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
In an adiabatic expansion, the temperature of one mole of an ideal monatomic gas ($\gamma = 5/3$) decreases from 60 K to 50 K. The work done by the gas in the process is:
(Take the universal gas constant as $R = 8.3$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$)
questions.sol:
Adiabatic work by gas $W = \dfrac{nR(T_1 - T_2)}{\gamma - 1} = \dfrac{1 \times 8.3 \times 10}{2/3}$.
$W = 124.5$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A ray of light with wavelength $\lambda$ is incident on three different photoelectric cells namely 1, 2 and 3. The threshold wavelength of these photoelectric cells are $\lambda_1$, $\lambda_2$, and $\lambda_3$, respectively and the magnitude of stopping potentials of these cells are $V_1$, $V_2$ and $V_3$, respectively. The relation between $\lambda$ and threshold wavelengths are $\lambda_1 < \lambda$, $\lambda_2 > \lambda$ and $\lambda_3 >> \lambda$. The correct option is:
questions.sol:
Emission needs $\lambda < \lambda_0$. For cell 1, $\lambda > \lambda_1$: no emission, $V_1 = 0$.
$eV = hc\left(\dfrac{1}{\lambda} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda_0}\right)$ grows with $\lambda_0$; since $\lambda_3 \gg \lambda$ while $\lambda_2$ is only greater than $\lambda$, $\lambda_3 > \lambda_2$ and so $V_3 > V_2$.
So $V_1 = 0,\ V_2 < V_3$.

questions.text:
A photon and an electron, each of 20 eV energy, move in free space. The ratio of linear momentum of electron $p_e$ to that of photon $p_{Ph}$, $\dfrac{p_e}{p_{Ph}}$ is:
[Take speed of light = $3 \times 10^8$ ms$^{-1}$, charge of electron = $-1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C and mass of electron = $9 \times 10^{-31}$ kg]
questions.sol:
$E = 20 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = 3.2 \times 10^{-18}$ J.
$p_e = \sqrt{2mE} = \sqrt{2 \times 9 \times 10^{-31} \times 3.2 \times 10^{-18}} = 2.4 \times 10^{-24}$ kg m/s; $p_{Ph} = E/c = 1.07 \times 10^{-26}$ kg m/s.
Ratio $= \dfrac{2.4 \times 10^{-24} \times 3 \times 10^8}{3.2 \times 10^{-18}} = 225$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Which of the following measurements require ‘index correction’?
options: Measurement of resistance of a wire using meter bridge
Measurement of gravitational acceleration using simple pendulum
Measurement of focal length of lenses using optical bench
Measurement of speed of sound using resonance tube
questions.sol:
Index correction is the correction for the difference between the actual distance between the uprights (needles/lens) and the separation read from the optical bench scale.
It is applied in focal-length measurements on an optical bench.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A unit positive point charge is taken slowly through an infinitesimally thin tube that is inside a charged dielectric sphere of radius $R$, having uniform positive charge density $\rho$, as shown in the figure. The initial and final positions of the charge are marked by $A$ and $B$ at distance $2R$ and $3R$ respectively, from the centre of the sphere. In this process, the magnitude of the total work done on the point charge is $\dfrac{\rho R^2}{n\varepsilon_0}$. The value of $n$ is :
($\varepsilon_0$ is the permittivity of vacuum)
questions.sol:
The field is conservative, so the work depends only on the end points, both outside the sphere.
Outside: $V(r) = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r}$ with $Q = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3\rho$, i.e. $V(r) = \dfrac{\rho R^3}{3\varepsilon_0 r}$.
$|W| = V(2R) - V(3R) = \dfrac{\rho R^2}{3\varepsilon_0}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\rho R^2}{18\varepsilon_0}$, so $n = 18$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Consider three media $P$, $Q$ and $R$ with refractive indices 1, 1.25, and 1.5 respectively. The medium $Q$ having a thickness of 5 cm is placed between extended media $P$ and $R$ as shown in the figure. An object $O$ is placed at the centre of medium $Q$. If viewed from medium $P$ near the normal direction, the apparent depth of $O$ is $h_1$. For similar observation from medium $R$, the apparent depth is $h_2$. The value of $|h_1 - h_2|$, in cm, is:
questions.sol:
Object is 2.5 cm from each face. Apparent depth $= d\,\dfrac{n_{\text{observer}}}{n_{\text{object}}}$.
$h_1 = 2.5 \times \dfrac{1}{1.25} = 2$ cm; $h_2 = 2.5 \times \dfrac{1.5}{1.25} = 3$ cm.
$|h_1 - h_2| = 1$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A frictionless circular wire of unit radius is fixed on the horizontal plane. Two-point particles of unit mass start moving simultaneously from point $A\left(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ with identical uniform angular speeds in opposite directions, and meet again at point $B\left(\theta = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. During this time, which of the following figures schematically represent the magnitude of the total linear momentum $P$ of the system, as a function of $\theta$?
questions.sol:
The particles are at mirror positions $\theta$ and $\pi - \theta$; their velocity components along the $AB$ line add while the perpendicular ones cancel.
$P = 2v|\cos\theta|$: zero at $\theta = \pi/2$, maximum $2v$ at $\theta = 0$, zero again at $\theta = -\pi/2$.
The curve is a single hump, graph (3).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The temperature of a metallic sphere of radius $R$ is increased by a small amount $\Delta T$. If the linear coefficient of thermal expansion of the metal is $\alpha$, the approximate increase in the volume of the sphere is:
questions.sol:
$\gamma = 3\alpha$, so $\Delta V = 3\alpha V\Delta T = 3\alpha \cdot \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \Delta T$.
$\Delta V = 4\pi R^3\alpha\Delta T$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A cylindrical cork of uniform density floats in a liquid of density $\rho_1$. If the cork is depressed slightly and released, it oscillates harmonically with time period $T$. If the same cork floats in another liquid of density $\rho_2$, then the similar oscillation has time period $2T$. The value of $\rho_2/\rho_1$ is:
questions.sol:
Restoring force for depression $x$: $F = -\rho A g x$, so $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{\rho A g}} \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\rho}}$.
Doubling $T$ needs $\rho$ to be one-fourth: $\rho_2/\rho_1 = 1/4$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: One main scale division of a Vernier calliper is equal to 1 mm and the number of divisions on the Vernier scale is 10. When both the jaws touch each other, the Vernier scale shifts to the left of zero of the main scale in such a way that 4$^{\text{th}}$ Vernier division coincides with a division of the main scale. If this Vernier calliper measures the length of the wire to be 1 cm, the actual length of the wire is :
questions.sol: NTA dropped this question (none of the options is exactly correct: the negative zero error is $-(10-4)\times 0.01 = -0.06$ cm, giving 1.06 cm); marks are given to all candidates.

questions.text: A solid sphere $A$ of radius $R$ and mass $M$ is attached at a point to a smaller solid sphere $B$ of radius $r < R$ and mass $m < M$. Assume that the line joining their centres lies along the horizontal. The moment of inertia of the system calculated about a vertical axis passing through the centre of $A$ is $I_A$ and that calculated about a vertical axis passing through the centre of $B$ is $I_B$. The difference $I_A - I_B$ is:
questions.sol:
Centres are $d = R + r$ apart.
$I_A = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 + \dfrac{2}{5}mr^2 + md^2$; $I_B = \dfrac{2}{5}mr^2 + \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 + Md^2$.
$I_A - I_B = (m - M)(R + r)^2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Consider a spring-mass simple harmonic oscillator in one dimension. The mass of the particle is $m$ kg and the spring constant is $k$ Nm$^{-1}$. At a given instant, the extension of the spring is $x$-meter and the speed of the particle is $v$ ms$^{-1}$. On the $x$ - $v$ plane, if the graph of $v$ as a function of $x$ is a circle, then the correct option is:
questions.sol:
Energy conservation: $\dfrac{1}{2}kx^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = E$, an ellipse in the $x$–$v$ plane.
It becomes a circle when the coefficients are equal (numerically): $k = m$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The lens combination as shown in the figure, consists of two lenses, $L_1$ and $L_2$, of the focal lengths +10 cm and – 10 cm, respectively. The position of the image formed is:
options: 20 cm to the left of the concave lens
60 cm to the left of the concave lens
30 cm to the right of the concave lens
60 cm to the right of the concave lens
questions.sol:
$L_1$: $u = -30$, $f = +10$: $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{30} \Rightarrow v = 15$ cm, i.e. 12 cm beyond $L_2$ (virtual object, $u = +12$).
$L_2$: $\dfrac{1}{v} = -\dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{12} = -\dfrac{1}{60} \Rightarrow v = -60$ cm.
Image is 60 cm to the left of the concave lens.

questions.text:
An ac voltage $V = 220\sin(2 \times 10^3 t)$ Volt is applied to a series LCR circuit. Then the current amplitude in this circuit is:
(Given : $L = 10$ mH, $C = 25\ \mu$F, $R = 100\ \Omega$)
questions.sol:
$X_L = \omega L = 2000 \times 0.01 = 20\ \Omega$; $X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{2000 \times 25 \times 10^{-6}} = 20\ \Omega$.
Resonance, so $Z = R = 100\ \Omega$ and $I_0 = 220/100 = 2.2$ A.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A thin horizontal disc is rotating about a vertical axis passing through its fixed centre $O$. Its angular momentum is $L_A$ and $L_B$ computed about points $A$ and $B$, respectively, with $OB = 2 \times OA$. The value of $\dfrac{L_A}{L_B}$ is:
questions.sol:
$\vec L_P = \vec L_{cm} + \vec r_{P\to cm} \times M\vec v_{cm}$.
The centre $O$ is fixed, so $\vec v_{cm} = 0$ and the angular momentum is the same about every point.
$L_A/L_B = 1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A conducting loop of finite resistance lies on the $x - y$ plane. There is a constant magnetic field in the $z$ direction. The area of the loop varies with time $t$, as $A = A_0(1 + \sin t)$ in appropriate units. The figure that correctly indicates the qualitative behaviour of the power $P$ dissipated in the loop as a function of time is:
questions.sol:
$\varepsilon = -\dfrac{d\Phi}{dt} = -BA_0\cos t$.
$P = \dfrac{\varepsilon^2}{R} = \dfrac{B^2A_0^2}{R}\cos^2 t$: maximum at $t = 0$, falls to zero at $t = \pi/2$, then rises again.
This is graph (2).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A point charge $Q$ is placed inside a cavity within a solid isolated conducting sphere. Consider points $A$, $B$ and $C$ as shown in the figure, where the magnitudes of the electric fields are $E_A$, $E_B$, $E_C$, respectively. The points $B$ and $C$ are at the same distance from the center of the solid sphere. The correct option is :
questions.sol:
Inside the cavity the field of $Q$ (and the induced charge on the cavity wall) is present, so $E_A \ne 0$.
Charge $+Q$ appears on the outer surface and spreads uniformly (the conductor shields the cavity), so outside the field is radial: $E = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2}$.
$B$ and $C$ are equidistant from the centre, so $E_B = E_C$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Consider a fixed uniformly charged insulating sphere with radius $R$ and total charge $+Q$. A point charge $-q$ ($q << Q$) with mass $m$ is released from rest at a distance of $3R$ from the centre of the charged sphere. When the point charge reaches the surface of the sphere, its speed is:
($\varepsilon_0$ is the permittivity of vacuum, neglect gravitational forces).
questions.sol:
Gain in KE = loss in PE: $\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = \dfrac{Qq}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{3R}\right) = \dfrac{2Qq}{12\pi\varepsilon_0 R}$.
$v^2 = \dfrac{Qq}{3\pi\varepsilon_0 mR}$, so $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{Qq}{3\pi\varepsilon_0 mR}}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In Geiger-Marsden experiment, the number of scattered $\alpha$-particles $N(\theta)$ is plotted as a function of scattering angle $\theta$. Which of the following options represents the correct plot?
questions.sol:
Rutherford's formula: $N(\theta) \propto \dfrac{1}{\sin^4(\theta/2)}$.
Most particles go nearly undeflected; the count falls steeply as $\theta$ increases and only a few scatter near $180^\circ$.
This is graph (3).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Consider two circuits, (A) and (B), each having two resistors. One of them has a positive temperature coefficient of resistance, $+\alpha$, while the other one has a negative temperature of coefficient, $-\alpha$, as shown in the figure. The current through these circuits are denoted by $I_A$ and $I_B$. At initial temperature, the resistance of the two resistors is $R_0$. As the temperature is increased, the correct option that describes the variation of current in these circuits is:
questions.sol:
(A) series: $R_0(1 - \alpha\Delta T) + R_0(1 + \alpha\Delta T) = 2R_0$, constant, so $I_A$ is constant.
(B) parallel: $R_{eq} = \dfrac{R_0^2(1 - \alpha^2\Delta T^2)}{2R_0} = \dfrac{R_0}{2}(1 - \alpha^2\Delta T^2)$, which decreases.
So $I_B$ increases.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Consider that $\sigma_s$, $k_B$, $b$ represents Stefan-Boltzmann constant, Boltzmann constant and Wien’s displacement law constant, respectively. The dimension of $\sigma_s k_B^{-1} b$ is
questions.sol:
$[\sigma_s] = \mathrm{MT^{-3}K^{-4}}$ (W m$^{-2}$K$^{-4}$), $[k_B] = \mathrm{ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}}$, $[b] = \mathrm{LK}$.
$\dfrac{\mathrm{MT^{-3}K^{-4}} \cdot \mathrm{LK}}{\mathrm{ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}}} = \mathrm{L^{-1}T^{-1}K^{-2}}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An electromagnetic wave travelling in a lossless dielectric medium having a dielectric constant, $\varepsilon_r = 9$, has the electric field, $E_x = E_0\sin(kz - 2\pi \times 10^6 t)$ Vm$^{-1}$ where $E_0$ is the amplitude and $k$ is the wave vector. Among the following options, the $\textbf{incorrect}$ choice is
options: The speed of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium is $10^8$ ms$^{-1}$
The wavelength of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium is 300 m
The magnetic field is given by the relation $B_y = \dfrac{B_0}{v}\sin(kz - 2\pi \times 10^6 t)$ where $v$ is the speed of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium
The direction of propagation of the electromagnetic wave is along $+z$
questions.sol:
$v = c/\sqrt{\varepsilon_r} = 10^8$ m/s, so (1) is correct; the phase $kz - \omega t$ means travel along $+z$, so (4) is correct.
$f = 10^6$ Hz, so $\lambda = v/f = 100$ m, not 300 m: (2) is incorrect.
The amplitude of $B_y$ should be $B_0 = E_0/v$; writing $B_0/v$ is also wrong, so (3) is incorrect. NTA accepts both (2) and (3).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: One mole of an ideal monatomic gas undergoes a cyclic process as shown in the figure. The total heat supplied to the gas is:
questions.sol:
Over a complete cycle $\Delta U = 0$, so net heat = net work = area of the cycle.
The cycle $a \to b \to c \to d$ is clockwise: $W = (300 - 100)(5 - 2) = 600$ J.
Net heat supplied $= 600$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Consider that an electron is revolving in an excited state of Hydrogen atom with velocity $\sqrt{25.6} \times 10^5$ ms$^{-1}$. The radius of the orbit is $x \times 10^{-9}$ m. The value of $x$ is:
[Take the mass of electron to the $9 \times 10^{-31}$ kg, charge of electron = $-1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C and $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9$ Nm$^2$C$^{-2}$]
questions.sol:
Coulomb force gives the centripetal force: $\dfrac{mv^2}{r} = \dfrac{ke^2}{r^2} \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{ke^2}{mv^2}$.
$r = \dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times 2.56 \times 10^{-38}}{9 \times 10^{-31} \times 25.6 \times 10^{10}} = 1 \times 10^{-9}$ m.
$x = 1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A car travels on a circular racetrack of radius 50 m, which is banked at an angle $\theta$. If the car travels at a speed 10 ms$^{-1}$, then the wear and tear on its tyres is minimum. Taking the acceleration due to gravity to be 10 ms$^{-2}$, the value of $\theta$ is:
questions.sol:
Minimum wear means no friction is needed: $\tan\theta = \dfrac{v^2}{rg}$.
$\tan\theta = \dfrac{100}{50 \times 10} = \dfrac{1}{5}$, so $\theta = \tan^{-1}(1/5)$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Three identical p-n junction diodes $D_1$, $D_2$, and $D_3$ are connected across a battery as shown in the figure. If the width of the depletion regions of $D_1$, $D_2$ and $D_3$ are $W_1$, $W_2$ and $W_3$, respectively, then the correct option is:
questions.sol:
$D_1$ is forward biased: its depletion layer narrows.
$D_2$'s branch is open, so no bias appears across it: equilibrium width.
$D_3$ is reverse biased: its depletion layer widens. Hence $W_3 > W_2 > W_1$.
questions.subject: Physics

The following table presents the part of the electromagnetic spectrum and their corresponding major applications.
Part of the electromagnetic spectrumApplications
P.MicrowaveI.For purifying the water
Q.UV raysII.For warming the food
R.Gamma raysIII.For AM and FM communication systems
S.Radio waveIV.For treating the Cancer cells
The $\textbf{correct}$ option is:
questions.sol: Microwaves heat food (P-II); UV kills germs in water purifiers (Q-I); gamma rays are used in cancer radiotherapy (R-IV); radio waves carry AM/FM broadcasts (S-III).

questions.text: Bob $B$ of mass $m$ at rest is hanging vertically from the ceiling via a massless string of length 10 m, as shown in the figure. Point mass $A$ of mass $m$ travelling horizontally with speed 10 ms$^{-1}$ hits bob $B$ elastically. The bob $B$ rises $h$ meter after the collision. Taking the acceleration due to gravity $g = 10$ ms$^{-2}$ and neglecting the size of the bob, the value of $h$ is:
questions.sol:
Elastic head-on collision of equal masses exchanges velocities: $B$ moves off at 10 m/s.
$h = \dfrac{v^2}{2g} = \dfrac{100}{20} = 5$ m (less than the string length, so the string stays taut).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An ideal gas is made of polyatomic molecules. Each of the molecules has three translational, three rotational and $f$ number of vibrational modes. If the ratio of heat capacities $C_P/C_V$ of the gas is 8/7, then the value of $f$ is:
questions.sol:
Each vibrational mode contributes $R$ (kinetic + potential) to $C_V$: $C_V = \left(\dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2} + f\right)R = (3 + f)R$.
$\gamma = 1 + \dfrac{R}{C_V} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{3 + f} = \dfrac{8}{7} \Rightarrow 3 + f = 7$.
$f = 4$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: For the following reaction sequence, choose the correct option.
options: If P is the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid, Q is a primary alcohol
P and Q are aromatic compounds
If P gives a carboxylic acid on acidification, Q gives a poisonous gas on exposure to air and light
Both P and Q are carbonyl compounds
questions.sol:
Friedel–Crafts acylation of benzene gives acetophenone, $\mathrm{C_6H_5COCH_3}$.
NaOCl brings about the haloform reaction: $\mathrm{C_6H_5COCH_3 \rightarrow C_6H_5COONa\ (P) + CHCl_3\ (Q)}$.
P on acidification gives benzoic acid; Q (chloroform) is oxidised by air in light to poisonous phosgene, $\mathrm{COCl_2}$. Hence option (3).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I : $\mathrm{[Fe(ox)_3]^{3-}}$ is chiral.
Statement-II : trans – $\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_2(ox)_2]^-}$ is chiral.
(Given : $\mathrm{oxH_2 = HOOC - COOH}$)
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{[M(AA)_3]}$ complexes such as $\mathrm{[Fe(ox)_3]^{3-}}$ have a propeller shape with no mirror plane, so they exist as $\Delta/\Lambda$ enantiomers – chiral (Statement-I correct).
In trans-$\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_2(ox)_2]^-}$ both oxalates lie in one plane, which is a mirror plane – achiral (Statement-II incorrect).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The following carbocation is stabilized by the interaction of the empty $p$ orbital with
questions.sol:
An empty orbital is stabilised only by donation from filled orbitals.
The benzylic cation is stabilised by resonance (overlap with the filled $\pi$ orbitals of the ring) and by hyperconjugation with the filled C–H $\sigma$ orbitals of the $\mathrm{CH_3}$ group.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: In potash alum, the ratio of $\mathrm{K^+}$ and $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ ions is
questions.sol:
Potash alum is $\mathrm{K_2SO_4\cdot Al_2(SO_4)_3\cdot 24H_2O}$, i.e. $\mathrm{KAl(SO_4)_2\cdot 12H_2O}$.
It contains 2 $\mathrm{K^+}$ for 4 $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$, so $\mathrm{K^+ : SO_4^{2-}} = 1 : 2$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The correct statement about peptides and proteins is
options: Tertiary structure of proteins has two or more polypeptide subunits
Only the proteins having a quaternary structure are biologically active
In $\beta$-pleated sheet structures, peptide chains are held together by intermolecular hydrogen bonds
In $\alpha$-helices, the polypeptide chain is twisted into a left-handed screw (helix) through intramolecular hydrogen bonds
questions.sol:
Two or more subunits define quaternary, not tertiary, structure, and many single-chain proteins are active, so (1) and (2) are wrong.
The $\alpha$-helix is a right-handed helix, so (4) is wrong.
In a $\beta$-pleated sheet, neighbouring chains are joined side by side by intermolecular hydrogen bonds, so (3) is correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The numbers 17.0145 and 21.0235 were rounded to three figures after the decimal point. The resulting numbers, respectively, are
questions.sol:
When the digit dropped is exactly 5, the preceding digit is left unchanged if it is even and increased by 1 if it is odd.
17.0145: the preceding digit 4 is even, so 17.014.
21.0235: the preceding digit 3 is odd, so 21.024.

questions.text:
The correct order of solubility of the given salts in water at 298 K is
Salt$K_{sp}$ at 298 K
$\mathrm{AgBr}$$5.0\times10^{-13}$
$\mathrm{Zn(OH)_2}$$1.0\times10^{-15}$
$\mathrm{Hg_2Cl_2}$$1.3\times10^{-18}$
questions.sol:
AgBr (1:1): $s = \sqrt{5.0\times10^{-13}} \approx 7.1\times10^{-7}$ M.
$\mathrm{Zn(OH)_2}$ (1:2): $s = (K_{sp}/4)^{1/3} = (2.5\times10^{-16})^{1/3} \approx 6.3\times10^{-6}$ M.
$\mathrm{Hg_2Cl_2 \rightleftharpoons Hg_2^{2+} + 2Cl^-}$: $s = (3.25\times10^{-19})^{1/3} \approx 6.9\times10^{-7}$ M.
So $\mathrm{Zn(OH)_2 > AgBr > Hg_2Cl_2}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Among the following options, the correct trend in the electron gain enthalpy is
questions.sol:
The magnitude of electron gain enthalpy generally falls down the group, but F is an exception.
Because F is very small, the added electron is strongly repelled by the crowded 2p electrons, so F releases less energy than Cl.
Order: Cl > F > Br > I.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Assertion A: For an ideal solution formed by mixing liquids P and Q, $\Delta_{mix}H = 0$ and $\Delta_{mix}V = 0$
Reason R: No interactions occur between P and Q
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
questions.sol:
For an ideal solution, $\Delta_{mix}H = 0$ and $\Delta_{mix}V = 0$, so A is correct.
P and Q do interact. In an ideal solution the P–Q interactions are equal in strength to the P–P and Q–Q interactions, so R is wrong.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The amino acid that gives a red-blood colour on treating its sodium fusion extract with sodium nitroprusside is
questions.sol:
The sodium nitroprusside test on the Lassaigne extract detects sulphur, which is present as $\mathrm{Na_2S}$.
Leucine, threonine and serine contain only C, H, N and O. Methionine, $\mathrm{CH_3SCH_2CH_2CH(NH_2)COOH}$, contains S.
So methionine is the only one that gives a positive test.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The standard electrode potential (E°) for the half-cell reaction $\mathrm{Fe^{3+} + e^- \rightarrow Fe^{2+}}$ at 298 K is
(Given : $E^\circ(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}/Fe}) = -0.04$ V and $E^\circ(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}/Fe}) = -0.44$ V at 298 K)
questions.sol:
Add free energies: $\mathrm{Fe^{3+} + 3e^- \rightarrow Fe}$: $\Delta G^\circ = -3F(-0.04) = +0.12F$.
$\mathrm{Fe \rightarrow Fe^{2+} + 2e^-}$: $\Delta G^\circ = +2F(-0.44) = -0.88F$.
Sum: $\mathrm{Fe^{3+} + e^- \rightarrow Fe^{2+}}$, $\Delta G^\circ = -0.76F = -1\cdot F E^\circ$, so $E^\circ = +0.76$ V.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: In an acidic medium, 10 mL of 0.25 M oxalic acid is titrated with $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ solution. If the volume of $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ solution required to reach end point is 10 mL, the strength of the $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ solution is
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{2MnO_4^- + 5H_2C_2O_4 + 6H^+ \rightarrow 2Mn^{2+} + 10CO_2 + 8H_2O}$.
Moles of oxalic acid $= 0.25\times10 = 2.5$ mmol, so $\mathrm{KMnO_4} = \tfrac{2}{5}\times2.5 = 1.0$ mmol.
Molarity $= 1.0/10 = 0.10$ M.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: According to crystal field theory, the correct order of ligands with respect to their decreasing order of field strength is
questions.sol:
In the spectrochemical series, $\mathrm{Cl^- < H_2O < NH_3 < CO}$.
CO, a $\pi$-acceptor, is the strongest of these ligands and the halide is the weakest. So in decreasing order: $\mathrm{CO > NH_3 > H_2O > Cl^-}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Two moles of an ideal gas undergo free expansion from 10 L to 100 L at 300 K. The values of $\Delta S_{system}$ and $\Delta S_{surroundings}$ are
(R is universal gas constant)
questions.sol:
Entropy is a state function, so for the gas $\Delta S_{sys} = nR\ln\dfrac{V_2}{V_1} = 2R\ln 10 = 2\times2.303R = 4.606R$.
In a free expansion no heat is exchanged with the surroundings ($q = 0$, $w = 0$), so $\Delta S_{surr} = 0$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: $2\mathrm{A}\xrightarrow{k}\mathrm{B}$ is a zero-order reaction, where $k = 1.0\ \mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}\ min^{-1}}$. If the initial concentration of A is 2 M, then the time taken to complete 75% of the reaction will be
questions.sol:
For $2\mathrm{A}\rightarrow\mathrm{B}$, rate $= -\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[\mathrm{A}]}{dt} = k$, so [A] falls at the rate $2k = 2.0\ \mathrm{M\ min^{-1}}$.
75% of 2 M is 1.5 M of A consumed: $t = 1.5/2.0 = 0.75$ min.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Generally, 3$d$ transition metals have high melting points.
Reason R: Involvement of 3$d$-electrons in addition to 4$s$-electrons in the interatomic metallic bonding.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct
questions.sol:
In transition metals, unpaired $(n-1)d$ electrons join the $ns$ electrons in metallic bonding. This gives strong metallic bonds and so high melting points.
Both A and R are correct, and R explains A.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
For a salt XY, which is a strong electrolyte, the plot of $\Lambda_m$ versus $\sqrt{c}$ has a slope of $-90.0\ \mathrm{S\ cm^2\ mol^{-3/2}\ L^{1/2}}$ at 298 K. At 0.01 M concentration of XY, the value of $\Lambda_m$ is $145.0\ \mathrm{S\ cm^2\ mol^{-1}}$. The limiting molar conductivity of $\mathrm{Y^-}$ ion ($\lambda^0_{\mathrm{Y^-}}$, in $\mathrm{S\ cm^2\ mol^{-1}}$) at 298 K will be
(Given : $\lambda^0_{\mathrm{X^+}} = 74.0\ \mathrm{S\ cm^2\ mol^{-1}}$)
questions.sol:
Kohlrausch: $\Lambda_m = \Lambda_m^0 - A\sqrt{c}$, so $145.0 = \Lambda_m^0 - 90.0\times\sqrt{0.01} = \Lambda_m^0 - 9.0$, which gives $\Lambda_m^0 = 154.0$.
$\lambda^0_{\mathrm{Y^-}} = 154.0 - 74.0 = 80.0\ \mathrm{S\ cm^2\ mol^{-1}}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The amount of carbon dioxide evolved upon complete combustion of 116 g of n-butane is
(Given: atomic mass in amu H = 1, C = 12 and O = 16)
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{2C_4H_{10} + 13O_2 \rightarrow 8CO_2 + 10H_2O}$.
Molar mass of butane = 58 g/mol, so 116 g = 2 mol, which gives 8 mol $\mathrm{CO_2}$.
Mass $= 8\times44 = 352$ g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
For an elementary chemical reaction, the Arrhenius plot is given below.
If the energy of activation is 6.64 kJ mol$^{-1}$ and R = 8.3 J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$, the temperature at which the rate constant becomes $e^2$ min$^{-1}$, is
questions.sol:
$\ln k = \ln A - \dfrac{E_a}{RT}$. The intercept (at $1/T = 0$) is $\ln A = 6$.
For $k = e^2$: $2 = 6 - \dfrac{6640}{8.3\,T}$, so $\dfrac{800}{T} = 4$ and $T = 200$ K.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement-I : Heating NaCl with concentrated $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ and $\mathrm{MnO_2}$ results in oxidation of Mn.
Statement-II : Heating NaI with concentrated $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ and $\mathrm{MnO_2}$ results in reduction of Mn.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{MnO_2}$ acts as the oxidant: $\mathrm{2X^- + MnO_2 + 4H^+ \rightarrow X_2 + Mn^{2+} + 2H_2O}$ (X = Cl or I).
In both cases Mn is reduced from +4 to +2 while the halide is oxidised.
So Statement-I (oxidation of Mn) is wrong and Statement-II is correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Among the species given below, the spin-only magnetic moment is highest for
(Given: Atomic number of Ti = 22, Mn = 25, Fe = 26 and Co = 27)
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ $d^4$ with strong-field $\mathrm{CN^-}$: $t_{2g}^4$, 2 unpaired electrons.
$\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ $d^5$ low spin: 1 unpaired. $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ $d^6$ low spin: 0. $\mathrm{Ti^{3+}}$ $d^1$: 1.
Maximum unpaired electrons (2, $\mu = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83$ BM) in $\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}$.

The lanthanide ion having four unpaired electrons is
(Given : Atomic numbers of Ce = 58, Nd = 60, Tb = 65 and Ho = 67)
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Ln^{3+}}$ configurations: $\mathrm{Ce^{3+}}$ $4f^1$ (1 unpaired), $\mathrm{Nd^{3+}}$ $4f^3$ (3), $\mathrm{Tb^{3+}}$ $4f^8$ (6), $\mathrm{Ho^{3+}}$ $4f^{10}$ (4).
So $\mathrm{Ho^{3+}}$ has four unpaired electrons.

questions.text: The formula of tetraammineaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride is
questions.sol:
The coordination sphere has 4 $\mathrm{NH_3}$, 1 $\mathrm{H_2O}$ and 1 $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ around $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$, giving charge $+3 - 1 = +2$.
Two chloride counter-ions are needed: $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_4(H_2O)Cl]Cl_2}$.

questions.text:
Consider the reversible processes for 1.0 mol of an ideal gas as shown in the figure.
$w_1$, $w_2$, $w_3$ and $w_4$ represent work done (in calories) in the processes 1, 2, 3 and 4, respectively; $\Delta U_2$ and $\Delta U_4$ are changes in the internal energy for the processes 2 and 4, respectively.
[use R = 2 cal K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$]
The correct option is
questions.sol:
Processes 1 ($T_1$) and 3 ($T_2$) are reversible isothermal: $w = -nRT\ln\dfrac{V_f}{V_i}$ with $nR = 2$ cal K$^{-1}$.
So $w_1 = -2T_1\ln\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}$ and $w_3 = -2T_2\ln\dfrac{V_4}{V_3}$, and their sum is option (1).
For the adiabatic steps, $w_2 = \Delta U_2$ and $w_4 = \Delta U_4 = -\Delta U_2$, so (2) fails. (3) has the wrong sign and omits $w_2$. The net work of a cycle is not zero, so (4) fails.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: The first ionization enthalpy of O is lower than that of N and F.
Reason R: The loss of an electron from O leads to stable half-filled $p$ orbital
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct
questions.sol:
O is $2p^4$. Removing one electron gives the stable half-filled $2p^3$ configuration, so O ionises more easily.
N already has a stable half-filled $2p^3$ shell, and F has a higher effective nuclear charge. Both have higher IE than O.
A is true and R correctly explains it.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the solutions formed by mixing two liquids.
A. An ideal solution thus formed obeys Raoult’s law throughout the composition range.
B. Mixture of chloroform and acetone shows negative deviation from Raoult’s law.
C. Mixture of aniline and phenol shows positive deviation from Raoult’s law.
questions.sol:
A: true by definition of an ideal solution.
B: true. Chloroform forms H-bonds with the C=O of acetone, so the mixture shows negative deviation.
C: false. Phenol forms strong H-bonds with the N of aniline, so the deviation is negative, not positive.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: One of the products formed in the following reaction is
questions.sol:
A Grignard reagent is a very strong base. It removes the acidic N–H proton of cyclohexylamine instead of adding to it.
$\mathrm{C_6H_{11}MgBr + C_6H_{11}NH_2 \rightarrow C_6H_{12} + C_6H_{11}NHMgBr}$.
So cyclohexane (option 4) is a product.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The correct statement is
options: Boron has a maximum covalency of four.
Magnesium has a maximum covalency of four.
questions.sol:
Second-period elements have only four valence orbitals (one 2s and three 2p), so boron can form at most four bonds, as in $\mathrm{[BF_4]^-}$. Statement (1) is correct.
Be also has four valence orbitals, not three.
Mg and Al can use 3d orbitals, so their maximum covalency is above four; Al has 3s, 3p and 3d orbitals, not five.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A protein undergoes reversible thermal denaturation from its initial state N to denatured state D according to $\mathrm{N \rightleftharpoons D}$. At 60ºC, the concentrations of both N and D are equal at equilibrium, and the standard enthalpy change of denaturation is 666 kJ mol$^{-1}$. The standard entropy change ($\Delta S^\circ$ in kJ K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$) of the protein upon denaturation at 60ºC is closest to
questions.sol:
[N] = [D] means $K = 1$, so $\Delta G^\circ = -RT\ln K = 0$.
Then $\Delta S^\circ = \dfrac{\Delta H^\circ}{T} = \dfrac{666}{333} = 2.0\ \mathrm{kJ\ K^{-1}\ mol^{-1}}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match the species in List-I with their geometry in List-II.
List-IList-II
A.$\mathrm{PCl_5}$I.Tetrahedral
B.$\mathrm{BrF_5}$II.Square Planar
C.$\mathrm{BF_4^-}$III.Trigonal bipyramidal
D.$\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$IV.Square pyramidal
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{PCl_5}$: $sp^3d$, 5 bond pairs, trigonal bipyramidal (III).
$\mathrm{BrF_5}$: 5 bond pairs + 1 lone pair, square pyramidal (IV).
$\mathrm{BF_4^-}$: $sp^3$, tetrahedral (I).
$\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$: $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ $d^8$ with a strong field, $dsp^2$, square planar (II).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : trans-But-2-ene upon treatment with $\mathrm{Br_2}$ in $\mathrm{CCl_4}$ gives the following product.
Statement II : cis-But-2-ene upon treatment with alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ gives the following product.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Br_2}$ adds anti. Anti addition to trans-but-2-ene gives meso-2,3-dibromobutane.
In the Newman projection of Statement I, the Br atoms are anti but the two Me groups are not related by a centre of symmetry, so it shows one enantiomer of the (±) form. Statement I is incorrect.
Cold alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ adds two OH groups syn. Syn addition to cis-but-2-ene gives meso-butane-2,3-diol.
Rotating the rear carbon of the Statement II projection to put the two OH groups anti puts Me opposite Me and H opposite H through a centre of symmetry, so it is meso. Statement II is correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Consider the following reaction sequences and choose the correct option.
options: K and L are geometrical isomers
M and N are geometrical isomers
questions.sol:
Na/liq. $\mathrm{NH_3}$ reduces the alkyne by anti addition to (E)-1-phenylpropene (L). Lindlar's catalyst gives syn addition and the (Z)-alkene (K). So K and L are geometrical isomers.
HBr/peroxide adds through the more stable benzylic radical, giving $\mathrm{PhCH_2CHBrCH_3}$ (N).
Ionic HBr adds through the benzylic cation, giving $\mathrm{PhCHBrCH_2CH_3}$ (M).
M and N are position isomers, not stereoisomers.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The complex which has facial and meridional isomers is
(Given : py = pyridine and en = $\mathrm{H_2N - CH_2 - CH_2 - NH_2}$)
questions.sol:
Fac/mer isomerism occurs in octahedral complexes of the type $\mathrm{[MA_3B_3]}$.
$\mathrm{[Cr(py)_3Cl_3]}$ is of this type: the three Cl can lie on one face (fac) or around a meridian (mer).
The other complexes are $\mathrm{MA_6}$, $\mathrm{MA_4B_2}$ (cis/trans) and $\mathrm{M(AA)_2B_2}$ (cis/trans).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Identify the reactions which give aniline as the major product.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.sol:
A: $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$ reduces $\mathrm{C_6H_5CN}$ to benzylamine, $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2NH_2}$, not aniline.
B: Hofmann bromamide degradation of benzamide gives aniline.
C: $\mathrm{NaBH_4}$ does not reduce an aromatic nitro group.
D: acid hydrolysis of acetanilide gives aniline (as its salt) and acetic acid.
So B and D only.

C.vitamin EIII.green leafy vegetables

questions.sol:
2,2-Dimethylcyclopentanone can form an enolate only at C-5, its only $\alpha$-$\mathrm{CH_2}$.
Crossed aldol with PhCHO followed by dehydration gives the 5-benzylidene ketone as E and Z isomers, options (2) and (4).

Conjugated double bonds alternate with a single bond, C=C–C=C.
