questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I : Oxidation of p-nitrotoluene with acidic $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ gives an acid that is stronger than benzoic acid.
Statement-II : Reduction of p-nitrotoluene with Sn/HCl followed by neutralization gives an amine that is more basic than aniline.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.sol:
Oxidation gives p-nitrobenzoic acid. The electron-withdrawing $\mathrm{-NO_2}$ group stabilises the carboxylate, so it is a stronger acid than benzoic acid.
Reduction gives p-toluidine. The electron-donating $\mathrm{-CH_3}$ group (+I and hyperconjugation) makes it more basic than aniline.
Both statements are correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The green paramagnetic species formed by heating $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ at 513 K is
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{2KMnO_4 \xrightarrow{513\,K} K_2MnO_4 + MnO_2 + O_2}$.
Manganate, $\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-}}$ (Mn +6, $d^1$), is green and paramagnetic with one unpaired electron.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Consider the following reaction, and choose the correct option.
options: On treating compound P with saturated $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ solution, brisk effervescence is observed
Compound P can be prepared by treating benzene with anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3COCl}$
On treatment with bromine water, compound P gives a white precipitate
Compound P is obtained by the hydrogenation of benzoyl chloride with Pd on $\mathrm{BaSO_4}$
questions.sol:
The Étard reaction ($\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2}$, then hydrolysis) oxidises toluene to benzaldehyde, P.
Benzaldehyde is not an acid, so no $\mathrm{CO_2}$ with $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$. Benzene with $\mathrm{CH_3COCl}$ gives acetophenone. The white precipitate with bromine water is a test for phenol/aniline.
Rosenmund reduction ($\mathrm{H_2}$, Pd/$\mathrm{BaSO_4}$) of benzoyl chloride gives benzaldehyde, so (4) is correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A 1 : 3 electrolyte in an aqueous solution is
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3 \rightarrow [Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+} + 3Cl^-}$ gives one complex cation and three anions, a 1 : 3 electrolyte.
The others are 1 : 1, 1 : 2 and a non-electrolyte, respectively.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following schematic plots of orbital wavefunction ($\psi_r$) against distance (r) from the nucleus.
The figure representing two radial nodes in the orbital is
questions.sol:
A radial node is a point at $r > 0$ where $\psi_r$ changes sign.
A: no crossing (0 nodes, e.g. 1s). B: one crossing (e.g. 2s). C: crosses zero twice (2 radial nodes, e.g. 3s). D: starts at zero at $r = 0$, which is not a radial node, and crosses once (e.g. 3p).
Answer: C.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of polarity
A. $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OCH_2CH_3}$
B. $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH}$
C. $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$
D. $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.sol:
Diethyl ether, with a weakly polar C–O–C, is the least polar.
Acetone has a strongly polar C=O.
Ethanol is more polar still because its O–H can hydrogen-bond.
Acetic acid, with both C=O and O–H, is the most polar.
Order: A $<$ C $<$ B $<$ D.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The highest occupied molecular orbital for $\mathrm{Ne_2}$ is
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Ne_2}$ has 20 electrons: $\sigma_{1s}^2\sigma^{*2}_{1s}\sigma_{2s}^2\sigma^{*2}_{2s}\sigma_{2p_z}^2\pi_{2p}^4\pi^{*4}_{2p}\sigma^{*2}_{2p_z}$.
The last orbital filled is $\sigma^*_{2p}$, which is the HOMO (bond order 0).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The number of vertebrae in a human is ________.
questions.sol: The adult human vertebral column has 26 vertebrae. They are 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 1 sacrum (5 fused) and 1 coccyx (4 fused). The numbers 7 and 12 are only the cervical and thoracic counts, and 206 is the total number of bones in the skeleton.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Symbiotic association between fungi and algae are called ________.
questions.sol: A lichen is a mutualistic partnership between an alga (phycobiont), which makes food, and a fungus (mycobiont), which gives shelter and absorbs water and minerals. Mycorrhiza is a fungus–plant-root association, sponges are animals and chrysophytes are protists.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Cell theory was formulated by _____________.
questions.sol: Matthias Schleiden (botanist, 1838) and Theodor Schwann (zoologist, 1839) together proposed the cell theory. Robert Brown discovered the nucleus, Singer and Nicolson gave the fluid mosaic model, and Leeuwenhoek first saw live cells.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Which of the following are characteristics of prokaryotic cells?
(a) Ribosomes are made of 50S and 30S subunits
(b) They can have plasmids
(c) They contain mesosome
(d) They have peroxisomes
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes made of 50S and 30S subunits, so (a) is correct. Many bacteria carry plasmids, so (b) is correct. Mesosomes are infoldings of the plasma membrane, so (c) is correct. Peroxisomes are membrane-bound organelles, which prokaryotes do not have, so (d) is wrong. The answer is (a), (b) and (c).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following is not a part of human central neural system?
questions.sol: The brain and spinal cord are covered by the meninges: the dura mater, arachnoid and pia mater. The pericardium is the membrane around the heart, so it is not part of the CNS.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Mitochondrial inner membrane encloses ___________ .
questions.sol: A mitochondrion has two compartments. The space inside the inner membrane is the matrix, which holds enzymes, circular DNA and 70S ribosomes. The outer compartment lies between the two membranes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
A.CristaeI.Flat membrane sacs in stroma of chloroplast
B.CisternaeII.Infoldings in mitochondria
C.ThylakoidsIII.Cell membrane
D.PhospholipidIV.Disc shaped sacs in the Golgi apparatus
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Cristae are infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane (A-II). Cisternae are the flat, disc-shaped sacs of the Golgi apparatus (B-IV). Thylakoids are flattened membrane sacs in the chloroplast stroma (C-I). Phospholipids form the bilayer of the cell membrane (D-III).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: The plastid that stores xanthophyll is known as __________.
questions.sol: Chromoplasts hold fat-soluble carotenoid pigments such as carotene and xanthophyll, which give yellow, orange or red colours. Amyloplasts store starch, aleuroplasts store proteins, and chloroplasts contain mainly chlorophyll.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Which of the following statements related to pituitary gland are correct?
(a) It is divided anatomically into adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis
(b) It secretes follicle stimulating hormone
(c) It secretes melanocyte stimulating hormone
(d) It does not secrete prolactin
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: The pituitary is divided into the adenohypophysis and the neurohypophysis, so (a) is correct. The pars distalis secretes FSH (and also prolactin), and the pars intermedia secretes MSH, so (b) and (c) are correct. Statement (d) is wrong because prolactin is a pituitary hormone. The answer is (a), (b) and (c).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Photorespiration reaction catalyzed by RuBisCo is shown below:
RuBP + $\mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow$ 3-Phosphoglycerate + X.
Identify “X” from the given options:
questions.sol: In photorespiration, RuBisCO acts as an oxygenase. It joins $\mathrm{O_2}$ to RuBP (5C) to give one 3-phosphoglycerate (3C) and one phosphoglycolate (2C). So X is 2-phosphoglycolate. PEP, OAA and malate belong to the $\mathrm{C_4}$ pathway.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Mad cow disease is caused by _______.
questions.sol: Mad cow disease (bovine spongiform encephalopathy) is caused by prions, which are abnormally folded infectious proteins. Viroids are free RNA agents that cause plant diseases such as potato spindle tuber.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which pigment has absorption peak at 700 nm in the photosynthetic reaction centre PS I (P700)?
questions.sol: The reaction centre of each photosystem is a special chlorophyll a molecule. In PS I it absorbs maximally at 700 nm (P700), and in PS II at 680 nm (P680). Chlorophyll b and the carotenoids are only accessory pigments.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: In water, frogs respire using _____________.
questions.sol: When a frog is in water, gas exchange takes place through its moist, highly vascular skin (cutaneous respiration). On land it uses the buccal cavity, skin and lungs.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of arrangement of bones in the lower limb of humans?
questions.sol: Going from proximal to distal: the femur (thigh), then the patella (knee cap) at the knee, then the tibia (with the fibula) in the leg, and then the tarsals at the ankle.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Phyllotaxy is the pattern of arrangement of ________.
questions.sol: Phyllotaxy is the pattern in which leaves are arranged on the stem or branch: alternate, opposite or whorled. The arrangement of flowers is called inflorescence.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
A.StarchI.Fights infection
B.AntibodyII.Energy storage
C.Concanavalin AIII.Glucose transport
D.Glut-4IV.Lectin
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Starch is a storage polysaccharide (A-II). Antibodies fight infection (B-I). Concanavalin A is a lectin (C-IV). GLUT-4 lets glucose into cells (D-III).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry.
Statement II : In phylum Echinodermata, both adults and larvae are radially symmetrical.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: Statement I is the correct definition of radial symmetry. Statement II is wrong because adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical but their larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Endomembrane system includes _______.
options: endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuole
endoplasmic reticulum, chloroplast, peroxisomes and vacuole
Golgi complex, chloroplast, peroxisomes and vacuole
questions.sol: The ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles work together, so they make up the endomembrane system. Mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes work independently and are not part of it.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are produced at the end of glycolysis from 206 molecules of glucose?
questions.sol: Glycolysis splits one glucose (6C) into two pyruvic acid (3C). So 206 glucose give $206 \times 2 = 412$ pyruvic acid molecules.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following plant growth regulators is used as herbicide?
questions.sol: 2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid) is a synthetic auxin. It kills dicot weeds but does not harm monocot crops, so it is widely used as a weedicide/herbicide.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes remain within the sporangia.
Statement II: In gymnosperms, seeds are not covered.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: In gymnosperms the gametophytes do not live freely. They stay inside the sporangia, which are retained on the sporophyte, so Statement I is correct. The ovules are not enclosed in an ovary, so the seeds are naked (gymnos = naked, sperma = seed), and Statement II is correct too.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
A.SphericalI.Vibrio
B.RodII.Cocci
C.CommaIII.Spirilla
D.SpirillumIV.Bacilli
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Bacterial shapes: spherical bacteria are cocci (A-II), rod-shaped are bacilli (B-IV), comma-shaped are vibrio (C-I), and spiral ones are spirilla (D-III).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Which of the following are characteristic features of Solanaceae family?
(a) Flowers are bisexual and actinomorphic
(b) Calyx have five sepals and are united
(c) Androecium have five stamens and are epipetalous
(d) Ovary is inferior
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Solanaceae flowers are bisexual and actinomorphic, with five united sepals (gamosepalous) and five epipetalous stamens, so (a), (b) and (c) are correct. The ovary is bicarpellary, syncarpous and superior, so (d) is wrong.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Select the correct sequence of experiments that led to a gradual understanding of photosynthesis in green plants.
options: Absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b $\rightarrow$ production of glucose $\rightarrow$ release of oxygen $\rightarrow$ role of air
Role of air $\rightarrow$ release of oxygen $\rightarrow$ production of glucose $\rightarrow$ absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
Release of oxygen $\rightarrow$ production of glucose $\rightarrow$ absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b $\rightarrow$ role of air
Production of glucose $\rightarrow$ role of air $\rightarrow$ release of oxygen $\rightarrow$ absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
questions.sol: Priestley (1770) first showed the role of air in a bell-jar experiment. Ingenhousz then showed that green parts release oxygen in sunlight. Sachs (1854) showed that glucose is produced and stored as starch. Engelmann later related the action spectrum to the absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: The number of action potentials generated by sino-atrial node (SAN) in a healthy human is _______ per minute.
questions.sol: The SA node is the pacemaker of the heart. It generates about 70–75 action potentials per minute, which sets the normal heart rate of about 72 beats per minute.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: How many turns of Calvin cycle are required for the formation of three molecules of glucose?
questions.sol: Each turn of the Calvin cycle fixes one $\mathrm{CO_2}$. One glucose ($\mathrm{C_6}$) needs 6 turns, so three glucose need $3 \times 6 = 18$ turns.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Blood coagulates in response to an injury
questions.sol: When there is an injury, thrombin converts soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin threads. These threads form the network of the clot. The reverse, fibrinogen made from fibrin, is incorrect.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
A.FamilyI.Sapindales
B.GenusII.Dicotyledonae
C.ClassIII.Anacardiaceae
D.PhylumIV.Angiospermae
E.OrderV.Mangifera
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: The classification of mango: genus Mangifera (B-V), family Anacardiaceae (A-III), order Sapindales (E-I), class Dicotyledonae (C-II), and phylum/division Angiospermae (D-IV). In plants the phylum level is called a division.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Arrange the following taxonomic categories in ascending order.
(a) Genus
(b) Class
(c) Order
(d) Phylum
(e) Family
(f) Kingdom
(g) Species
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: From the lowest rank to the highest: Species $\rightarrow$ Genus $\rightarrow$ Family $\rightarrow$ Order $\rightarrow$ Class $\rightarrow$ Phylum $\rightarrow$ Kingdom. This is (g), (a), (e), (c), (b), (d), (f).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
A.Marginal placentationI.Argemone
B.Axile placentationII.Tomato
C.Parietal placentationIII.Primrose
D.Free central placentationIV.Pea
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Pea has marginal placentation (A-IV). Tomato has axile placentation (B-II). Argemone has parietal placentation (C-I). Primrose (Primula) has free central placentation (D-III).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Sphenopsida class belongs to _____________.
questions.sol: Pteridophytes are divided into four classes: Psilopsida, Lycopsida, Sphenopsida (e.g. Equisetum) and Pteropsida. So Sphenopsida belongs to the pteridophytes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Which of the following statements regarding photorespiration are correct?
(a) Do not occur in C3 plants
(b) $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is consumed and $\mathrm{O_2}$ is generated
(c) Phosphoglycolate is formed
(d) No synthesis of ATP and NADPH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Photorespiration happens in $\mathrm{C_3}$ plants, so (a) is wrong. In it $\mathrm{O_2}$ is used up and $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is released, so (b) is wrong. RuBP oxygenation forms phosphoglycolate (c), and no ATP or NADPH is made (d). The answer is (c) and (d).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum ___________ .
options: has ribosomes attached to its surface
is the major site for the synthesis of lipids
is actively involved in protein synthesis
is a site for the synthesis of carbohydrates
questions.sol: SER has no ribosomes on its surface. It is the main site for making lipids, including lipid-like steroidal hormones in animal cells. Protein synthesis takes place on RER, which has ribosomes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
questions.sol: In the islets of Langerhans, $\alpha$-cells secrete glucagon, which stimulates glycogenolysis, and $\beta$-cells secrete insulin. So the statement that $\alpha$-cells secrete insulin is incorrect.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Genus represents __________.
options: a population of plants and animals
a group of closely related species
a group of closely related families
questions.sol: A genus is a group of related species that share more characters with each other than with species of other genera. For example, Panthera includes the lion, tiger and leopard. A group of related genera makes a family.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following is not a prokaryote?
questions.sol: Bacteria, blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) and mycoplasma are prokaryotes in Kingdom Monera. Fungi have a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles, so they are eukaryotes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following plant growth regulators promotes internode elongation prior to flowering in cabbage?
questions.sol: Gibberellins cause bolting, which is the elongation of internodes just before flowering in rosette plants such as cabbage and beet.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: The correct sequence of adult cell cycle phases is ________.
questions.sol: Interphase comes first: G1 (growth), then S (DNA synthesis), then G2 (preparation for division). It is followed by the M phase (mitosis). So the order is G1–S–G2–M.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
A.Fusion of protoplasms between gametesI.Meiosis
B.Fusion of two nucleiII.Plasmogamy
C.Generation of haploid sporesIII.Karyogamy
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: In fungal sexual reproduction, protoplasm fusion is plasmogamy (A-II) and nuclear fusion is karyogamy (B-III). The zygote then undergoes meiosis to produce haploid spores (C-I).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : The class name Reptilia refers to creeping or crawling mode of locomotion.
Statement II : All organisms belonging to Reptilia have three chambered heart.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: The name Reptilia comes from the Latin repere/reptum, meaning to creep or crawl, so Statement I is correct. Most reptiles have a three-chambered heart, but crocodiles have a four-chambered heart, so Statement II ("all") is incorrect.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Chromosomes are fully condensed at the end of prophase I.
Statement II : Meiosis I resembles mitosis.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is true
questions.sol: By diakinesis, the last stage of prophase I, the chromosomes are fully condensed, so Statement I is correct. Meiosis II resembles mitosis, while meiosis I is reductional, so Statement II is false.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following is not a characteristic of chordates?
questions.sol: All chordates have a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord, paired pharyngeal gill slits and a post-anal tail at some stage of life. So absence of gills is not a chordate feature.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Length of the stem at time 0 is 20 cm. The arithmetic growth rate is 30 cm per day. What is the length of the stem at the end of the $7^{\text{th}}$ day?
questions.sol: Arithmetic growth follows $L_t = L_0 + rt$. Putting in the values, $L_7 = 20 + 30 \times 7 = 20 + 210 = 230$ cm.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Arrange the following elements in descending order of their contribution to percentage weight of the human body.
(a) Oxygen
(b) Carbon
(c) Hydrogen
(d) Nitrogen
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: By weight, the human body is about 65% oxygen, 18.5% carbon, 9.5% hydrogen and 3.3% nitrogen. So the descending order is (a), (b), (c), (d).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: In frogs, the number of pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain are ______.
questions.sol: Frogs (like other anamniotes) have 10 pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain. Humans and other amniotes have 12 pairs.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following is used as a clot buster?
questions.sol: Streptokinase, produced by Streptococcus, dissolves blood clots in the vessels of patients after myocardial infarction, so it is called a clot buster. Penicillin is an antibiotic, cyclosporin A is an immunosuppressant and statins lower blood cholesterol.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: The inactive form of Bt toxin is converted to the active form in the insect gut ________
questions.sol: Bt toxin exists as an inactive protoxin in the bacterium. Once ingested, the alkaline pH of the insect gut solubilises the crystals and converts the protoxin into the active toxin, which binds midgut epithelial cells and causes pores, lysis and death of the insect.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Down’s syndrome is caused by the absence of one of the X-chromosomes.
Statement II : Turner’s syndrome is caused by the presence of an additional copy of the chromosomes.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: Down’s syndrome is caused by an additional copy of chromosome 21 (trisomy 21), so Statement I is incorrect. Turner’s syndrome is caused by the absence of one X chromosome (45, XO), so Statement II is also incorrect. The two descriptions are swapped.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following disease is not sexually transmitted?
questions.sol: Syphilis, gonorrhoea and genital warts are sexually transmitted infections. Tuberculosis, caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, spreads mainly through airborne droplets and is not an STI.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Sperm motility is due to ___________.
questions.sol: A sperm has a tail that is a flagellum; mitochondria in the middle piece supply energy for its beating. Sperm motility is therefore due to flagellar movement.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Natural selection can lead to _________.
(a) stabilisation
(b) genetic drift
(c) directional change
(d) disruption
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Natural selection acting on a population can be stabilising, directional or disruptive. Genetic drift is a separate, chance-based mechanism of change in allele frequency and is not an outcome of natural selection. Hence (a), (c) and (d) only.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: The method of directly of injecting a sperm into ovum in assisted reproductive technology is called :
questions.sol: In ICSI (intra cytoplasmic sperm injection) a sperm is injected directly into the cytoplasm of the ovum to form an embryo in the laboratory. GIFT transfers gametes and ZIFT transfers a zygote into the fallopian tube.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following struture is not a part of the male reproductive system?
questions.sol: Rete testis, vasa efferentia and epididymis are male accessory ducts that carry sperm from the testis. The infundibulum is the funnel-shaped part of the fallopian tube (oviduct) in the female, so it is not part of the male system.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Arrange the following in descending order of number of species in the Amazonian rain forest.
(a) Plants
(b) Birds
(c) Fishes
(d) Invertebrates
(e) Mammals
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: The Amazonian rain forest has about 1,25,000 species of invertebrates, 40,000 plants, 3,000 fishes, 1,300 birds and 427 mammals. So the descending order is invertebrates $>$ plants $>$ fishes $>$ birds $>$ mammals, i.e. (d) $>$ (a) $>$ (c) $>$ (b) $>$ (e).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : Ovulation is caused by LH surge leading to rupture of Graafian follicles.
Statement II: Graafian follicle remaining after ovulation transform into corpus luteum and secretes large amount of estrogen.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: The mid-cycle LH surge induces rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of the ovum, so Statement I is correct. The remnants of the follicle form the corpus luteum, which secretes large amounts of progesterone (not estrogen), so Statement II is incorrect.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following are primary consumers in a food chain?
questions.sol: Primary consumers feed directly on producers (plants). Herbivores therefore occupy the second trophic level as primary consumers; carnivores are secondary or higher consumers.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: A population of diploid organisms is at Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. If the frequency of allele A is 0.1, the frequency of AA is ________.
questions.sol: At Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, genotype frequencies are $p^2 : 2pq : q^2$. With $p = 0.1$, frequency of AA $= p^2 = (0.1)^2 = 0.01$.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
(A)Excess growth hormone(I)Reabsorption of water and electrolytes in kidney
(B)Luteinizing hormone(II)Contraction of uterus during child birth
(C)Vasopressin(III)Acromegaly
(D)Oxytocin(IV)Ovulation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Excess GH in adults causes acromegaly (A-III). LH surge induces ovulation (B-IV). Vasopressin (ADH) promotes reabsorption of water and electrolytes in the distal tubules (C-I). Oxytocin causes contraction of uterine muscles during child birth (D-II).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: The opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle is guarded by ________.
questions.sol: The right atrioventricular opening is guarded by the tricuspid valve (three flaps). The bicuspid (mitral) valve guards the left atrioventricular opening, and semilunar valves guard the exits into the pulmonary artery and aorta.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Sponges exchange $\mathrm{O_2}$ with $\mathrm{CO_2}$ by __________.
options: simple diffusion over their entire body surfaces
questions.sol: Lower invertebrates such as sponges, coelenterates and flatworms have no special respiratory organs; they exchange $\mathrm{O_2}$ and $\mathrm{CO_2}$ by simple diffusion over their entire body surface. Moist cuticle is used by earthworms, tracheae by insects and gills by most aquatic arthropods and molluscs.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: How many theca are present in each lobe of a typical bilobed angiosperm anther ?
questions.sol: A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed and each lobe has two theca (dithecous). It therefore has four microsporangia in total.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system by the release of _____ .
questions.sol: A neural signal reaching the neuromuscular junction releases the neurotransmitter acetylcholine, which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma. This spreads through the muscle fibre and causes release of $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$ from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, starting contraction.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following statements about lac-operon is correct?
options: Lactose activates repressor to bind to the operator
Genes $i$, $z$, $y$ and $a$ share single common promoter
Galactose can act as an inducer of lac operon
questions.sol: The regulator gene $i$ has its own promoter and is expressed constitutively, producing the repressor all the time. Lactose (allolactose) inactivates, not activates, the repressor; only $z$, $y$ and $a$ share the lac promoter; and the inducer is lactose, not galactose.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following in female gametophyte of an angiosperm helps in guiding the pollen tube for fertilizing the eggs?
questions.sol: The synergids, lying beside the egg at the micropylar end, bear a filiform apparatus that guides the pollen tube into the synergid. Antipodals, the central cell and polar nuclei have no guiding role.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following plant produces non-albuminous seeds?
questions.sol: In non-albuminous (ex-albuminous) seeds the endosperm is fully consumed during embryo development, as in pea and groundnut. Wheat, maize and barley retain endosperm and are albuminous seeds.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: If the diploid chromosome number of typical angiosperm is 36, what would be the chromosome number in its endosperm?
questions.sol: $2n = 36$, so $n = 18$. The endosperm is triploid ($3n$), formed by fusion of a male gamete with two polar nuclei: $3 \times 18 = 54$.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Which of the following statements about the reabsorption process in Henle's loop are correct?
(a) The descending limb of Henle's loop is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes.
(b) Urine gets concentrated in Henle's loop.
(c) Reabsorption of $\mathrm{Na^+}$ and water takes place in Henle's loop.
(d) Active or passive transport of electrolytes occurs in the ascending limb of Henle's loop.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: (a) is correct: the descending limb is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes. (b) is correct: the filtrate becomes concentrated as it moves down the descending limb. (d) is correct: the ascending limb transports electrolytes actively or passively while being impermeable to water. (c) is incorrect because the two limbs differ — $\mathrm{Na^+}$ and water are not reabsorbed together, and overall reabsorption in Henle's loop is minimal. Hence (a), (b) and (d) only.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct order of arrangement of vertebrate column from the head to toe?
options: Cervical vertebra, thoracic vertebra, sacrum, lumbar vertebra
Sacrum, lumbar vertebra, thoracic vertebra, cervical vertebra
Cervical vertebra, lumbar vertebra, thoracic vertebra, sacrum
Cervical vertebra, thoracic vertebra, lumbar vertebra, sacrum
questions.sol: From the skull downwards the vertebral column has 7 cervical, 12 thoracic and 5 lumbar vertebrae, followed by the sacrum (fused) and the coccyx. So the order is cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacrum.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following is not evidence for evolution?
options: Convergent evolution of traits like wings of birds and butterflies
Embryological support for evolution as proposed by Ernst Heckel
Divergent evolution of anatomical structures such as forelimbs
questions.sol: Fossil records, homologous structures (divergent evolution) and analogous structures (convergent evolution) are all accepted evidences of evolution. The embryological support proposed by Ernst Haeckel (that embryos of higher animals pass through adult stages of lower animals) was disproved by Karl Ernst von Baer, so it is not accepted evidence.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Modern Homo sapiens arose in Australia and moved across continents.
Statement II : Homo sapiens arose around 75000 to 10000 years ago.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: Modern Homo sapiens arose in Africa and migrated across continents, so Statement I is incorrect. During the ice age between 75,000 and 10,000 years ago modern Homo sapiens arose, so Statement II is correct.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Consider a population of 10 million cells. Given the per-capita birth rate of 0.002 (per unit time) and the per-capita death rate of 0.002 (per unit time), the expected number of cells after 10 generations is ______.
questions.sol: Intrinsic rate of increase $r = b - d = 0.002 - 0.002 = 0$. With $r = 0$, $dN/dt = rN = 0$, so the population neither grows nor declines and remains 10 million.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: During PCR, primers bind to the DNA strands in the ______step.
questions.sol: A PCR cycle has three steps: denaturation (strands separate at high temperature), annealing (the mixture is cooled and primers bind to complementary sequences on the single strands) and extension (Taq polymerase extends the primers). Primer binding is annealing.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A : The logistic growth model of populations is considered more realistic than the exponential growth model.
Reason R : Resources are finite.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
questions.sol: No population has unlimited resources, so growth eventually slows and levels off at the carrying capacity $K$. The logistic (Verhulst-Pearl) model includes this limit and is therefore more realistic than the exponential model. Both statements are true and the finiteness of resources explains A.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Adaptive radiation in placental mammals and Australian Marsupials leading to similarity between distant species is an example of ________.
questions.sol: When adaptive radiation occurs separately in two isolated groups (placental mammals and Australian marsupials) and produces similar forms, such as the placental wolf and the Tasmanian wolf, unrelated lineages come to resemble each other. This is convergent evolution.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Which of the following are secondary lymphoid organs?
(a) Bone marrow
(b) Tonsils
(c) Spleen
(d) Thymus
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Bone marrow and thymus are primary lymphoid organs where lymphocytes are produced and mature. Spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer’s patches and MALT are secondary lymphoid organs where lymphocytes interact with antigens. Hence (b) and (c) only.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following hormone is not secreted by human placenta?
questions.sol: The placenta acts as an endocrine tissue producing hCG, hPL, estrogens and progestogens (and relaxin late in pregnancy). LH is secreted by the anterior pituitary, not by the placenta.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following enzymes synthesizes precursor mRNA?
questions.sol: In eukaryotes RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S, 5.8S), RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs, and RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA (hnRNA).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Plasmids are autonomously replicating DNA.
Statement II : Plasmids are extrachromosomal DNA.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: Plasmids are small circular DNA molecules present outside the bacterial chromosome (extrachromosomal) and they carry their own origin of replication, so they replicate autonomously. Both statements are correct.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: For a person with blood group ‘O’, which of the following is not a possible combination of parents’ blood group genotypes?
questions.sol: A child with blood group O has genotype $ii$ and must receive an $i$ allele from each parent. In options (1)–(3) both parents carry $i$. In option (4) the father is $I^AI^B$ and has no $i$ allele, so an $ii$ child is impossible.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A : Forelimbs of human and bats are homologous.
Reason R : Forelimbs of humans and bats have similar anatomical structure.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.sol: The forelimbs of humans and bats perform different functions but share the same basic anatomical plan (humerus, radius-ulna, carpals, metacarpals, phalanges). Organs with similar structure and common origin are homologous, so R correctly explains A.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Colostrum, secreted by mother during initial days of lactation, is abundant in ________.
questions.sol: The yellowish colostrum secreted in the first few days of lactation is rich in IgA antibodies, which give the newborn passive immunity.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A : Abingdon tortoise in Galapagos islands became extinct within a decade after goats were introduced.
Reason R : Goats were more efficient at browsing than Abingdon tortoise.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
questions.sol: This is a classic example of interspecific competition: the Abingdon tortoise became extinct within a decade of goats being introduced on the island, apparently because of the greater browsing efficiency of the goats. Both statements are correct and R explains A.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: The covering of ovum at ovulation is _________.
questions.sol: The secondary oocyte released at ovulation is surrounded by a non-cellular glycoprotein layer, the zona pellucida (with corona radiata cells outside it). The endometrium lines the uterus, and the chorion is an extra-embryonic membrane formed later.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
A.Both species are harmedI.Predation
B.One species is harmed and the other is benefitedII.Mutualism
C.Both species are benefitedIII.Competition
D.One is benefited while the other has no effectIV.Commensalism
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Competition harms both species ($-/-$): A-III. Predation benefits the predator and harms the prey ($+/-$): B-I. Mutualism benefits both ($+/+$): C-II. Commensalism benefits one with no effect on the other ($+/0$): D-IV.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A : In an experiment, Mendel observed that the F1 progeny plants are all tall and none are dwarf.
Reason R : Stem height is a contrasting trait, with tall being dominant and dwarf being recessive.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
questions.sol: In Mendel’s monohybrid cross ($TT \times tt$) all F1 plants are $Tt$ and tall, none dwarf. This is because tall is dominant over dwarf for the contrasting trait of stem height, so the dwarf allele is not expressed in the heterozygote. R correctly explains A.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A : In recombinant DNA technology, lysozyme is used for disrupting bacterial cells while cellulase is for plant cells.
Reason R : Isolation of genetic material needs disruption of cells.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
questions.sol: To isolate DNA, the cell must first be broken open to release it. Lysozyme digests the bacterial cell wall and cellulase digests the plant cell wall, so these enzymes are used for cell disruption. R gives the reason for using them, so both are correct and R explains A.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following is used as an effective sedative and painkiller for treating post-surgery patients?
questions.sol: Morphine, an opioid extracted from the latex of the poppy plant, is a very effective sedative and painkiller and is useful for patients who have undergone surgery.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are Correct ?
(a) Energy flow from producers to consumers is unidirectional
(b) Energy pyramid can never be inverted
(c) Transfer of energy follows the 1% law
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Energy flows one way from producers to consumers (a is correct). Since energy is lost as heat at every step, the pyramid of energy is always upright (b is correct). Transfer between trophic levels follows the 10% law, not 1% (c is incorrect). Hence (a) and (b) only.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct about Plasmodium?
options: Fertilization takes place in mosquito gut
questions.sol: In humans Plasmodium multiplies asexually in liver cells and RBCs, and gametocytes develop in the RBCs. When a female Anopheles takes up the gametocytes, fertilisation occurs in the mosquito gut and the sexual phase continues there.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
A.TransformationI.Restriction enzyme
B.Cloning siteII.Transfer DNA to host bacteria
C.SelectionIII.Replication
D.OriIV.Antibiotic
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Transformation is the introduction of DNA into host bacteria (A-II). A cloning site is a recognition site for a restriction enzyme (B-I). Selection of transformants uses antibiotic-resistance markers (C-IV). Ori is the origin of replication (D-III).
